canonical_definition: Instruction Following Behavior refers to a system's capability to understand and execute tasks based on given instructions, typically involving multimodal inputs (e.g., language, visual data) and generating task-specific outputs across domains like code generation, visual chat, robotics, and audio processing. It is commonly evaluated through success rates in controlled benchmarks (e.g., MT-Bench, AlpacaEval) and in-the-wild generalization tests, with performance influenced by instruction tuning, alignment strategies, and coherence maintenance to mitigate hallucinations. Poor instruction following correlates with incoherent responses, semantic conflicts, and failures in discrimination tasks, while robust implementations enable long-horizon planning and task induction in complex environments.
